text1: When the Gates went dark, every credit in the Sector became a claim no one could verify. Only the Persean Fiscal Office, a minor Domain treasury annex at Aurum, still held a complete copy of the Sector's accounts. Three cycles after the Collapse it joined the surviving merchant houses of Varenne, Okonkwo-Lisle and Tessaly to sign the Bullion Charter, and the Persean Banking Confederation was born. Its articles are short: the Ledger is one, every debt is recorded, the Confederation takes no side, and it defends its books, not its borders.
text2: Two centuries later the Confederation clears trade between factions that will not speak to each other, underwrites the bonds that fund their wars, and keeps the credit file of every captain it deals with. Its branch offices are neutral ground by treaty. Those who default meet the Collection Fleets of the Recovery Directorate, which hail before they fire and return larger when destroyed. Spacers say the PBC has never lost a war, because it has never fought one - it has only ever collected.

text1: Bullion is the administrative heart of the Persean Banking Confederation. Its arcologies house the Clearing Hall, the Board of Houses and hundreds of thousands of clerks, auditors and actuaries. The world has no great industry; its export is trust, and per capita it is the richest world in the Sector.

An airless rock that holds the Ledger: the original Domain fiscal data cores, buried kilometres below the surface among redundant archives, reserves of rare metals and automated defences that answer to no single officer. Three keys open the deep archive - the High Director's, the Chief Auditor's and the Fleet Director's. Officially, no one has turned all three since the Charter was signed.

Ledger's gas mining and the refineries of Ledger Station fuel the Confederation's fleets and keep its day-to-day operations independent of its own clients. The founders insisted on it: a bank that cannot fuel its own fleet is a bank that can be starved.
